Find that the proposed actions in the agenda report are categorically
exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act ("CEQA"), pursuant to State
CEQA Guidelines Section 15301

exempt class, and therefore, there are no unusual circumstances;

authorize the City Manager to
enter into a three-year contract with a total not-to-exceed amount of $338,990,

percent contingency of $56,498

  Richard McDonald, representing the appellant, noted that a
  mitigated categorical exemption relating to asbestos is not allowed
  for the proposed project, and emphasized that the project cannot be
  determined as categorically exempt without further analysis.

  Todd Nelson, on behalf of the applicant, noted that there is
  substantial evidence in the public hearing record to support the City's
  determination that the project is eligible for categorical exemption.

  In response to Mr. McDonald's concerns related to asbestos,
  Councilmember Lyon noted that other projects in the City that were
  advocated by Mr. McDonald are also not subject to conditions of
  approval for breaking pavement. In response to Mr. Johnson's
  (appellant) comments regarding school pick-up/drop-offas a primary
  existing traffic congestion issue, Councilmember Lyon noted that the
  traffic congestion is a pre-existing condition that is tied to the school
  and not the proposed project, and raised the question whether the
  existing traffic congestion prevents all other additional developments
  from occurring nearby. Mr. Johnson (appellant) suggested that the
  ingress and egress point to the project be placed on Green Street
  instead of Holliston Avenue to alleviate some traffic congestion.

Council Minutes  12  03/02/2026
   Mayor Gordo stated that the proposed project site could be used for
  alterative purposes, such as a commercial use, which may create

n
  more traffic than the proposed research and development project.

  In response to Councilmember Lyon's inquiry regarding biosafety
  levels ("BSL") of the proposed project, Ms. Moses stated that the
  applicant would allow the City to condition the project that it remains
  in perpetuity as a BSL 1 or 2 laboratory environment.

  Planning Director Paige reported that the proposed project is in a
  commercial zone that has existed since the 1970s, and after being
  incorporated into the East Colorado Specific Plan in 2022 as part of
  the Mid-City Innovation District, the zone allows a wide range of uses
  including commercial, mixed-use, research and development, and
  residential development. She also reported information on the City's
  ordinance, adopted in 2024, establishing special regulations for
  research and development uses, allowing benefits like additional
  height, FAR exceptions, and eliminating the need for a major project
  CUP so projects can proceed by-right with only design review.

  In response to Councilmember Lyon's inquiry regarding possible
  alternatives that could occur on the site, Planning Director Paige and
  Luis Rocha, Planning Manager, reported that commercial or
  residential projects, such as a 100% affordable housing project
  without density maximums, could be developed at the site.

  In response to Councilmember Lyon's inquiry regarding the general
  oversight framework for research and development uses at a local
  level, Timothy Cell, Deputy Fire Chief, reported that in addition to the
  oversight from various agencies at the federal and state levels,
  supplemental regulations are enforced by the City's municipal code,
  the City's Fire Department, and the City's Environmental Health and
  Safety Division.

  In response to Councilmember Cole's inquiry regarding the City's
  authority in terms of traffic mitigation, Joaquin Siques, Director of
  Transportation, clarified that enforceable authority is limited during
  normal operations because the City does not set conditions on when
  vehicles may enter/exit a building. He noted that City staff can work
  with the applicant and neighboring properties to encourage optimal
  timing but cannot mandate compliance.

  Councilmember Cole advocated for the City Council to consider
  additional regulations to protect the surrounding neighborhood and
  properties adjacent to the proposed project area.
